note: abstract and keywords missing in the converted text; the paper's percentages contain arithmetic errors

qs.q: Which dataset was used, how big is it, and how was it split and trained?
qs.a: EdNet-KT1: 131 million interactions from 784,309 students on 13,169 questions covering 188 concepts, 2017 to 2020; 167.6 questions per learner on average with 65.5% correct; split 70/15/15 into train, validation and test; 500 training episodes on an NVIDIA A100 80GB

qs.q: By how much did HRL-VCO beat the best baseline in accuracy, and what test supports the significance?
qs.a: 91.4% vs 86.3% for SAKT, 5.1 percentage points, paired t-test p<0.001 (number of runs or seeds not given)

qs.q: The paper says the mean reward of 266.3 is 34.2% greater than the best flat RL baseline, PPO at 218.4. Does the table support 34.2%?
qs.a: No. (266.3-218.4)/218.4 is about 21.9%, not 34.2%. The 34.2% figure is repeated in the Conclusion

qs.q: Which ablation hurt most, according to Table 2, and does the paper's text agree?
qs.a: Removing the LSTM learner-state encoder: accuracy 79.3, mean reward 156.2, knowledge gain 19.1, much worse than removing hierarchy (85.7, 218.4, 26.8). The text first says hierarchy ablation gives the biggest degradation, then says the LSTM ablation gives the strongest one (-12.1% accuracy), so it contradicts itself

qs.q: What do the ablation figures such as -5.7% accuracy and -12.1% accuracy mean?
qs.a: Percentage points of absolute difference from the full model (91.4-85.7=5.7; 91.4-79.3=12.1), not relative percentages; the mean-reward drop of -18.0% is a relative change

qs.q: How does the 'HRL-VCO w/o Hierarchy' row compare with the flat PPO baseline row?
qs.a: The numbers are identical (accuracy 85.7, mean reward 218.4, knowledge gain 26.8), so the single-level ablation and the PPO baseline report the same results

qs.q: Was the system tested with real students in a live classroom?
qs.a: No. All experiments are on the historical EdNet logs; no live deployment is reported. The 34.7% 'knowledge gain' is a metric from the experimental setup, yet the paper presents it as real-world educational effectiveness and says it could reduce dropout, which was not measured

qs.q: What limitations do the authors state?
qs.a: Evaluation relies on clickstream and response records and ignores emotional and physiological states; the method needs large datasets such as EdNet, which may be a barrier for small organisations

qs.q: What confidence intervals or random-seed counts back the numbers in Table 1?
qs.a: NOT STATED. Only a paired t-test p-value for accuracy is given

qs.q: What is the inference latency of HRL-VCO per student decision?
qs.a: NOT STATED. No latency or deployment timing is reported
